To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zinc polycarboxes are a good luting agent for crowns but are not as good as glass ionomer cement.

(1) the mechanical properties of the zinc polycarboxes are comparable with those of the calcium hydroxide cements; (2) the solubilities of the zinc polycharboxylate are low; (3) the adhesion to enamel is comparable with that of zinc oxyphosphate cement; and (4) the adhesion is better than that of calcium hydroxide cement.

the mechanical properties, setting time and solubility of zinc polycarbonate cements depend on the composition, and the apparent pH of setting, film thickness and enamel adhesion depend on the composition and the method of preparation of the cement paste.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and evaluation of a series of zinc polycarbonate cements.
the development of a range of polycarboxylic acid salts as cements for use in dentistry.
the synthesis, characterisation and evaluation of polycarboxylic acids and their zinc salts as dental cements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zinc polycarboxes are suitable as luting agents but are not suitable for use as linings, and this is so whether they are used as cements or as pastes.
the properties of the zinc polycarboxes are not as yet sufficiently well understood to enable them to be formulated to give a predictable and reliable performance.
the cements have a wide range of properties which make them suitable for use as both linings and lute.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cements containing 1.0-2.5% by weight of polycarboxylic acid, 0.5-3.0% by weight of zinc oxide, 1.0% by wt of glycols and 0.5% by wt of water are suitable as linings and as luting agents.
the cements are not suitable as luting agents, but may be used for lining cavities.
cements containing a mixture of polyacrylic and polyitaconic acids give the best combination of properties for use in dentistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the zinc polycar-boxylate cement is a very versatile material, which can be used in a wide range of clinical situations.
the cements are generally satisfactory as liners, but that their use for luting purposes is limited.
the properties of polycarboxylic acids are not as good as the manufacturer's claim.
